ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE THE ACTING CHIEF JUSTICE MR. JUSTICE A.J.DESAI)
1. By way of the present petition, the petitioner has prayed as under:
"[A] Your Lordships may be pleased to admit and allow this petition.

[B] Your Lordships may be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus, or a writ in the nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or direction quashing and setting aside order dated 5.2.2005 at Annexure A passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11901/2023 ORDER DATED:
14/07/2023 undefined Himmatnagar; and further be pleased to remand the matter with a direction to decide the same afresh on merits after affording opportunity of hearing to the petitioner."

2. Facts in brief are as under:
2.1 It is the case of the petitioner that he was the owner of agricultural land bearing block no.347 paiki at village:Sakaria, District:Aravalli.
Out of the total land i.e. 2-08-84 H-Are-Sq.Mtrs., 0-25-14 H-Are-Sq.Mtrs. land was acquired for Village:Sakaria-NAPA road construction.
Section 4 notification was published on 05.01.1999.
According to the petitioner, the award came to be published on 30.06.1999.
Aggrieved by the insufficient compensation, the petitioner preferred the reference.
The application under Section 18 has been rejected as being time barred by the order impugned in this petition which is dated 05.02.2005.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11901/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/07/2023 undefined 3.
Mr.R.C.Jani learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the application filed under Section 18 was rejected on account of delay.
It is submitted that the order is bad.
He would submit that the order dated 05.02.2005 rejecting the application could not have been passed as the application under Section 18 could not have been preferred by the petitioner earlier.
The petitioner was waiting for the decision of the Court in the case of surrounding land owners whose reference was decided on 16.04.2021.

4. Having heard Mr.R.C.Jani learned advocate for the petitioner and having perused the order impugned in the petition, it is clear that as recorded in the order, the publication of the award was on 12.07.2000.
Notice under Section 12(2) was served on 23.06.2000.
Compensation was paid on 27.06.2000.

Reference was filed on NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11901/2023 ORDER DATED:
14/07/2023 undefined 10.08.2000.

In other words, from 23.06.2000 i.e. the date on which notice under Section 12(2) was issued and served, there has been a delay of 49 days for making an application under Section 18.
5.
In context of the prayer made in the petition, what is evident is that the order impugned is challenged after a period of 18 years.

Even otherwise, reading Section 18(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, it is apparent that an application stating grounds on which objection to the award is taken, has to be filed within a period of six weeks from the date of the Collector's award.
In other cases, the same has to be filed within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under Section 12(2).

Admittedly, as recorded in the impugned order, Section 12(2)

2

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/11901/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/07/2023 undefined notice was served on 23.06.2000 and the application was filed under Section 18 beyond the period of 42 days on 10.08.2000.
It was therefore beyond the prescribed period of time as provided under the provisions of Section 18 of the Act.
6. Perusal of the petition would indicate that no sufficient explanation as to why the petition has been filed after such gross delay.
On this ground alone, the petition deserves to be dismissed.
7. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.
(A.J.DESAI, ACJ) (BIREN VAISHNAV, J)
